title: Checks for iterating a map (HashMap or BTreeMap) and ignoring either the keys or values.
summary: Readability. There are keys and values methods that can be used to express that don’t need the values or keys. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for unbounded for loops over char or integers.
summary: Using a unbounded range over char and integers will unexpectedly not handle overflows so it will lead to panics or infinite loops. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for calls to std::mem::forget with a value that does not implement Drop.
summary: Calling std::mem::forget is no different than dropping such a type. A different value may have been intended. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of .map(|_| format!(..)).collect::<String>().
summary: This allocates a new string for every element in the iterator. This can be done more efficiently by creating the String once and appending to it in Iterator::fold, using either the write! macro which supports exactly the same syntax as the format! macro, or concatenating with + in case the iterator yields &str/String. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Detects format! within the arguments of another macro that does formatting such as format! itself, write! or println!.
summary: Suggests inlining the format! call. The recommended code is both shorter and avoids a temporary allocation. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: Detects cases where the result of a format! call is appended to an existing String.
summary: Introduces an extra, avoidable heap allocation. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for outer doc comments written with 4 forward slashes (////).
summary: This is (probably) a typo, and results in it not being a doc comment; just a regular comment. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.
